data.narrative:
SambaNova Systems is a Series F semiconductor chip design company founded by Rodrigo Liang, Kunle Olukotun, and Christopher Ré, currently valued at $11.0B post-money on $1.1B total capital raised. The valuation assessment draws from a comp universe of 11 peers across Chips & Semiconductors—3 public (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private entities including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, Etched, Ayar Labs, and Tenstorrent, which span valuations from $2.3B to $39.2B.

Two triangulation methods proved applicable. Stage-Progression analysis, applying a typical 1.3x step-up multiplier from Series F forward, implies $14.3B valuation. Peer-Median analysis across the 7 same-sector comparables with similar valuation tier yields a median of $3.8B, though this reflects significant dispersion (range: $2.3B–$39.2B) driven by public outliers Cerebras ($39.2B) and Credo ($35.8B). Public-Comp Anchoring proved inapplicable; while the semiconductor sector median P/S stands at 20.4x across public tickers, SambaNova's revenue is not publicly disclosed. 

The triangulated range spans $3.2B (low) to $16.4B (high), with a median of $9.0B. The current $11.0B valuation sits in the upper half of this range, between the Stage-Progression floor and peer-median anchors. Key uncertainties include the wide dispersion in peer comparables and SambaNova's undisclosed revenue, limiting precision of public-market calibration.
